title.narrative: Skills for life and work in the LAC region

description.narrative: The project aims to strengthen skills for life and work in Chile through the adaptation and implementation of the European Union’s Centres of Vocational Excellence (CoVE) model within the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector. The initiative responds to key challenges such as high youth unemployment, labor informality, and the mismatch between training provision and labor market needs. Through at least two pilot institutions, UNESCO Santiago will provide technical assistance to promote high-quality technical education, with a strong focus on digital transformation and the integration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. The model is built around four core components: governance, capacity development, curriculum and learning content, and ecosystem partnerships. It also promotes continuous professional development for teachers, skills development for students, and lifelong learning opportunities. The initiative is guided by the principles of innovation, inclusion, digital transformation, and continuous improvement. Implemented in partnership with DUOC UC and other national and international stakeholders, the project seeks to establish a scalable model that enhances youth employability while contributing to local economic development and stronger connections between education, industry, and public policy.
